rules: When `mstateen0.CTR=0` and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access `sctrctl`, `vsctrctl`, `sctrdepth`, or `sctrstatus` raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When `mstateen0.CTR=0` and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access `sireg*` when `siselect` is in the range 0x200 through 0x2FF raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When `mstateen0.CTR=0` and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, execution of the `SCTRCLR` instruction raises an illegal-instruction exception.
When Supervisor Counter Delegation is enabled and an attempt to access `scountinhibit` is made from VS-mode or VU-mode, a virtual-instruction exception is raised.
When counters are not delegated to S-mode, the bits in `scountinhibit` are read-only zero.
If implementations support Smcdeleg/Ssccfg, Sscofpmf, and the H extension, attempting to read `scountovf` from VS-mode or VU-mode raises a virtual-instruction exception when `menvcfg.CDE=1`.
If `mstateen0.CTR=1` and `hstateen0.CTR=0`, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state or VSmode execution of `SCTRCLR` raise a virtual-instruction exception.
When `mstateen0.CTR=1` and `hstateen0.CTR=1`, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state behave as described in Section 7.2 and Section 11.2.

If CTR is active (current privilege mode is enabled for recording and CTR is not frozen) and a qualified control transfer occurs, the Entry Registers are updated at logical entry 0, and `ctrsource.V` is set to 1.
If the CTR buffer is full, the oldest recorded entry is lost upon a qualified control transfer.
Execution of the `SCTRCLR` instruction zeroes all CTR Entry Registers for all DEPTH values.
Execution of the `SCTRCLR` instruction zeroes the CTR cycle counter and CCV.
A read of `ctrsource`, `ctrtarget`, or `ctrdata` following `SCTRCLR` but preceding the next qualified control transfer returns 0.
The first recorded transfer following `SCTRCLR` will have `ctrdata.CCV=0`.
When `sctrstatus.FROZEN=1`, transfer recording is inhibited.
If `sctrctl.LCOFIFRZ=1` and a local-counter-overflow interrupt (LCOFI) traps to M-mode or S-mode, `sctrstatus.FROZEN` is set by hardware.
If `sctrctl.BPFRZ=1` and a breakpoint exception traps to M-mode or S-mode, `sctrstatus.FROZEN` is set by hardware.
If CTR is active, the `CtrCycleCounter` increments at the same rate as the `mcycle` counter.

When CTR is active, the `CC` field is encoded such that CCE holds 0 if the `CtrCycleCounter` value is less than 4096, otherwise it holds the index of the most significant one bit in the `CtrCycleCounter` value, minus 11, and CCM holds `CtrCycleCounter` bits CCE+10:CCE-1.
Writing to `x ctrctl` or execution of `SCTRCLR` resets the `CtrCycleCounter`, ensuring accumulated cycle counts do not persist across a context switch.
